title: PyUL_SK: PyUltraLight 2 SK fork for black holes in ultralight dark matter solitons (v30.50)
description:
PyUL_SK is the fork of PyUltraLight 2 used for the black-hole simulations of Stone Skipping Black Holes in Ultralight Dark Matter Solitons (A. Zhang, Y. Wang, J. L. Zagorac and R. Easther, arXiv:2602.11512). It is a pseudo-spectral (split-step Fourier) solver for the Schroedinger-Poisson equations of ultralight dark matter coupled to N-body point masses (black holes), with cell-centred grids, manual dynamical friction, isolated or periodic potentials, a resampled centre-of-mass cube for eigenmode analysis, and an optional inline decomposition into soliton eigenmodes, c_nlm(t), computed while the simulation runs (with the companion ULDM-Eigenmode-Toolkit).

Release 30.50 is a maintenance release of the 30.40 core used for part of the paper runs. With default options it reproduces 30.40 bit for bit, except the resampled-cube outputs, which LegacyResampleBox=True reproduces. It adds packaging, tests, laptop and PBS/Slurm examples, support for Python 3.9 to 3.14 with NumPy 2 and current SciPy, safe non-interactive behaviour on clusters, complete provenance records, and many bug fixes. CHANGELOG.md lists every change; docs/known_issues_and_errata.md documents the bugs of older versions and their effect on the paper's figures.

Lineage and credits: PyUltraLight by F. Edwards, E. Kendall, S. Hotchkiss and R. Easther (JCAP 10 (2018) 027, doi:10.1088/1475-7516/2018/10/027); PyUltraLight 2 / PyUL_NBody by Yourong F. Wang and collaborators (Auckland Cosmology; github.com/Sifyrena/PyUL_NBody, doi:10.5281/zenodo.6336160), on which this fork is built; SK fork by Alan Zhang. The NOTICE file records the origin of the code and reproduces the upstream BSD-style copyright notice; the fork's own changes are distributed under the MIT licence in LICENSE. Please also cite the upstream works and the paper listed in CITATION.cff.
